metadata.note: VM rehearsal of the ThinkPad P14s Gen 2 boot chain as it is declared in the personal config repo: a 2GiB ESP, an encrypted LUKS swap sized for hibernation, and an encrypted btrfs root carrying the full ten-subvolume layout shared with the desktop. Unlike config/vm-laptop-hibernate.json this declares NO rd.luks.name at all — the point is to prove KernelCmdlineAction derives one for BOTH encrypted partitions (the swap included, which is what makes resume possible) from `resume=` alone. Both volumes carry luks_options token-timeout=10s, the real machine's fallback-to-passphrase setting, to prove it does not break the passphrase path. unlock_fido2 is FALSE here and true on the real machine: systemd-cryptenroll runs with check=True, so enrolling a key that is not plugged in aborts the apply — FIDO2 can only be verified on real hardware. Public test passphrase 'hibpass' on both devices; autologins root over serial. Swap is 4GiB against the harness's 4096 MiB of RAM (the real machine's 32GiB does not fit in a VM image). NOT for real hardware.

files.content:
# Managed by dasik. Mirrors the real machine: closing the lid suspends and
# then hibernates, which only works because the swap is LUKS with a persistent
# key. HibernateDelaySec is deliberately unset — systemd's default sets the RTC
# alarm from the battery discharge rate.
[Login]
HandleLidSwitch=suspend-then-hibernate
HandleLidSwitchExternalPower=suspend
